subject: WebMCPify Core
object: an MIT-licensed TypeScript ESM CLI, confined stdio MCP server, and optional Temporal worker for creating and verifying WebMCP capabilities

subject: The normal Core workflow
object: discovers first, accepts optional non-authoritative product context, then security check, human review, approved apply, browser test, and independent verification; review permits tool selection only, with read-only contracts/tasks, collapsible sections, patch-file reasons, and source consent cleared/disabled on partial selection; rejecting tools directly removes independent inline JS/TS registrations using a lazily loaded parser in a disposable workspace, preserves ordinary app handlers and exact unaffected task IDs/setup/outcomes/criteria, drops rejected-only and mixed/dependent tasks, and regenerates retained-only docs; ambiguous/shared source or TypeScript unused-integration cleanup uses a focused coding provider, while missing retained-tool coverage or test-count shortfalls use a source-frozen task-only pass; initial and revised drafts require at least ceil(tool count times 1.3) valid tasks without a six-task ceiling, with every tool covered and extra unaffected tests preserved; providers may return only new-ID supplements, which Core merges with immutable retained tasks before validating the combined count and coverage; explicit TASKS_JSON blocks take precedence over unrelated examples; approved legacy sets remain readable and repair/durable reviews preserve fixed approved contracts/tasks; all revised drafts undergo build/wiring/feedback/security and source/patch identity checks before fresh human approval; one review server locks controls across tabs/refreshes, reports progress, reopens revised drafts, supports repeated removals and failed-provider retry with selections retained, and drains finalized connections after response flush; target URL must be provided or set through WEBMCPIFY_URL; invalid verification tasks can be discarded only if the resulting count contract and tool coverage still hold; success tasks declare multi-tool setup; grounded rejection tasks preserve the unmet prerequisite and require observed tool/error evidence plus independent unchanged-state verification

subject: Generated source changes
object: a disposable workspace and reach the target only as an exact human-approved patch; root/nested Serena state is excluded from workspace copies and captured patches, and patches targeting .serena are rejected without changing owner configuration; generation preserves JS/TS conventions, checks declarative form styling/status markers, and merges one root AGENTS.md combining repository instructions and detailed site capabilities with Improvisus/WebMCPify attribution; no second .agent.md is generated; root-served llms.txt/webmcp.md, static HTML capability guidance with truthful WebPage metadata, and scoped robots allowances are added when deployment is identifiable, separate from private run state; owner HTML/sections and crawler restrictions survive, README explains proposed capabilities, and an always-present deployment/GEO/AEO checklist covers real links/canonical/sitemap and search-versus-training controls without invented domains or indexing guarantees; wiring checks inspect current runtime files, not documentation or removed diff lines; preflight anchors package-manager paths, skips stale optional dependency links, disables pnpm automatic before-run installs only in validation subprocesses without purging linked target dependencies, and distinguishes missing executables or interactive-install environment failures from source validation while safely naming the failed check; failed apply/build checks or cancellation attempt rollback of patch paths, restoring originals/deletions/renames and removing newly introduced files using in-memory pre-apply classification unaffected by altered manifests; missing original backups never cause deletion of current source, other recoverable paths are still restored, and incomplete recovery retains evidence; post-success backup cleanup failure warns rather than rolling back; later browser failures, databases, payments, and arbitrary build side effects are not automatically undone

subject: Core security gating
object: balance by default for run, standalone generation, audits, and review fallback; standalone security --strict selects the strict audit policy and fails on blocking findings without changing an existing draft policy; review preserves explicitly recorded draft policies, and generate exposes balance|ignore|strict selection; balance checks high-impact actions and invalid cross-origin allowlists; strict reviews declared execution scope, input bounds, privacy, origins and applicable controls without imposing backend authorization or identity/replay/quota requirements on browser-local reversible UI state; backend mutations and consequential effects retain their applicable checks, and high-impact effects cannot bypass them through a UI label; every mode preserves exact-patch human approval

subject: Browser verification
object: each approved task on its exact acted-on tab in a fresh task context, preserving DOM/component state, cookies, session storage and navigation without resetting personal CDP authentication; test and baseline agents receive empty disposable workspaces and the MCP bridge shares the scorer's CDP endpoint; expected rejections still require tool/error evidence plus a postcondition; non-Claude allowlists remain instruction-level controls rather than a universal OS sandbox

subject: Target-owned run state
object: the target project's .webmcpify directory, including discovery, proposals, approvals, security reports, patches, evaluations, rollback, and trajectories; the owner must exclude it from Git and deployment because Core does not automatically enforce ignore policy; the combined root AGENTS.md and served llms.txt/webmcp.md are separate reviewed guidance files

subject: Temporal
object: optional and lazily loaded for durable repair/final evaluation; normal CLI/MCP paths work without its peers; worker and clients share address, namespace, queue and optional TLS/API-key settings; activities use operation-specific deadlines, heartbeats and propagated cancellation, with automatic side-effect retries disabled while explicit repair attempts remain; review is still an activity rather than signal-based approval and live backend/crash recovery is not certified

subject: Core development
object: strict TypeScript with NodeNext ESM, Node 20.19+ compatibility, pnpm, focused verification scripts, and the validation checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md

subject: Core security analysis
object: backend enforcement; universal provider attestation and production policy storage adapters remain unimplemented

subject: WebMCP and browser support
object: experimental and runtime-dependent, so availability must be detected rather than assumed

subject: Project memory
object: Barry Cache docs/context facts and ADRs; .codex project memory is retired and Serena remains a semantic code-navigation tool

subject: Provider generation
object: a provider-neutral output normalizer for raw text, JSON envelopes, JSONL events, nested assistant content, and future common response shapes; AGY uses accept-edits mode plus one edit-only retry for a text-only proposal; malformed tool/task metadata gets one metadata-only correction with source/Git identity and already-valid contract preservation, revalidation, and a canonical corrected review draft; failed corrections stop before publishing a pending proposal; provider executable paths are anchored before workspace changes, Codex has standalone/editor fallbacks, and safe launch errors distinguish missing executables, working directories, and interpreters while keeping raw diagnostics private

subject: Source action discovery and generation completeness
object: uncapped discovery signal lists and deterministic lazily parsed JS/TS/JSX candidates for named handlers/store actions, conditional branches, and multiline callbacks; unresolved references remain source-inspection hints and parse failures retain regex signals with warnings; generation has no fixed tool-count limit and accounts for resolved candidates using exact declared handler matches or CAPABILITY_COVERAGE_JSON mapping to proposed tools, discovered existing registrations, or explicit source-grounded omission reasons, never arbitrary count/budget skips; unaccounted actions get one source-capable completion in the disposable workspace, preserving existing valid contracts and Git identity, requiring source edits for added tools, and revalidating scaled tasks, wiring, build, security, and human approval; explicit omissions survive metadata-only correction in the reviewed draft; dynamic/aliased/non-JS handlers and declared coverage still require agent inspection and runtime verification, so static discovery is not an exhaustive proof; owner-rejected review selections are not globally recompleted
